nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm, humid summers on the Black Sea coast power plant growth across the reedbeds, bogs and wet forest.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: The Colchis plain is among the wettest parts of the region, with mild humid weather and abundant rain that keeps the lowlands waterlogged.

nodes.name: Waterlogged peat
nodes.desc: Peat layers built up over thousands of years underlie the bogs and marshes; they hold water and nutrients that the plants draw on.

nodes.name: Rivers and lake water
nodes.desc: Slow rivers, Lake Paliastomi and flooded marshes make up more than half of the protected area and carry water and nutrients across the plain.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead reeds, alder leaves and animals, returning nutrients to the peat and water.

nodes.name: Common alder
nodes.desc: Alders and willows form the deciduous wet forest on the Colchic plain, rooted in waterlogged soil.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Tall grass that forms dense reedbeds along lake shores and channels, giving food and cover to many wetland animals.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Sedges grow in the wet meadows and peat bogs; one of them, Carex lasiocarpa, is listed for the park's bogs.

nodes.name: Sphagnum moss
nodes.desc: Bog moss that carpets the peat bogs; its slowly decaying remains help build the thick peat layers.

nodes.name: Coypu
nodes.desc: Large semi-aquatic rodent, introduced to the area, that eats reed and other wetland plants.

nodes.name: European water vole
nodes.desc: Burrowing rodent of banks and wet meadows that feeds on reeds, sedges and grasses and is prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Ural field mouse
nodes.desc: Small ground-dwelling rodent recorded near the park; a staple prey for herons, harriers and mammals.

nodes.name: Green leafhopper
nodes.desc: Sap-feeding insect that lives on sedges, rushes and other herbs of damp ground.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: Small deer listed among the park's mammals; browses leaves and shoots in the wet forest and meadows.

nodes.name: Lesser emperor
nodes.desc: Large dragonfly of still and slow water that catches other insects in flight; its larvae live in the water.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: The most recorded amphibian near the park; it eats mostly insects and other invertebrates and is itself food for snakes, herons and otters.

nodes.name: Dice snake
nodes.desc: Water snake of rivers and lakes that hunts fish and amphibians.

nodes.name: Grey heron
nodes.desc: Wading bird that stalks shallow water for fish, frogs and small mammals; heavily recorded around the park.

nodes.name: Southern white-breasted hedgehog
nodes.desc: Ground-foraging insectivore recorded near the park; GloBI lists frogs, snakes, lizards and small rodents among its prey.

nodes.name: Western marsh harrier
nodes.desc: Raptor tied to reedbeds that glides low over marsh hunting small mammals, birds, frogs and reptiles.

nodes.name: Eurasian otter
nodes.desc: Semi-aquatic hunter listed among the park's mammals; eats mainly fish plus amphibians and small mammals.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: Elusive forest cat with only a single record near the park; it takes deer, hares and rodents.
